state.startup_desc: A precision-application platform for arable farms. Field sensors and satellite imagery produce zone-level pesticide maps, so growers treat only the parts of a field that need it instead of spraying the whole area.

Adoption chain.description: A field-sensor and satellite platform that tells arable growers which sub-field zones actually need pesticide, replacing blanket spraying with zone-specific application maps sent straight to the sprayer.
Adoption chain.assumption: Growers trust a zone map enough to spray less than their habitual full-field rate.

Adoption chain.description: 412 farms across 3 countries on paid subscriptions, covering 68,000 hectares. Adoption is evidenced by billing records and by sprayer telemetry confirming the maps were actually loaded.
Adoption chain.assumption: Subscribed hectares are genuinely farmed under the platform rather than signed up and left unused.

Adoption chain.description: Growers apply pesticide to a mean 61% of field area instead of 100%. Sprayer telemetry gives applied litres per hectare before and after onboarding for 289 of the 412 farms.
Adoption chain.assumption: The reduction persists beyond the first season and is not offset by growers re-treating zones later in the year.

Adoption chain.description: Lower pesticide load reaching soil and watercourses, plus lower upstream manufacturing emissions per hectare farmed. The baseline is the grower's own prior-season application record.
Adoption chain.assumption: Avoided application translates into proportionally avoided ecotoxicity, which the platform does not measure directly.

state.weakest_links: The step from reduced application to avoided ecotoxicity is the weakest link: it is inferred, not measured. The platform evidences litres not applied and treats avoided harm as proportional to that. Persistence of the behaviour change beyond a single season is also not yet evidenced.
